AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: This study aimed to develop and validate an in vitro dissolution method based on in silico-in vivo data to determine whether an in vitro-in vivo relationship could be established for rivaroxaban in immediate-release tablets.

AbstractText.Label: SIGNIFICANCE
AbstractText.content: Oral drugs with high permeability but poorly soluble in aqueous media, such as the anticoagulant rivaroxaban, have a major potential to reach a high level of in vitro-in vivo relationship. Currently, there is no study on scientific literature approaching the development of RIV dissolution profile based on its in vivo performance.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS AND RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Drug plasma concentration values were modeled using computer simulation with adjustment of pharmacokinetic properties. Those values were converted into drug fractions absorbed by the Wagner-Nelson deconvolution approach. Gradual and continuous dissolution of RIV tablets was obtained with a 30 rpm basket on 50 mM sodium acetate +0.2% SDS, pH 6.5 medium. Dissolution was conducted for up to 180 min. The fraction absorbed was plotted against the drug fraction dissolved, and a linear point-to-point regression (R2 = 0.9961) obtained.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The in vitro dissolution method designed promoted a more convenient dissolution profile of RIV tablets, whereas it suggests a better relationship with in vivo performance.
